title: Robust LLM-based Multi-Agent System with Action Negotiation and Sharing Redundancy Enhancement

problem.claim: Internal conflicts and insufficient information sharing among agents can cause global-level failures in LLM-based multi-agent systems, particularly under abnormal conditions or adversarial attacks.

gap.claim: The robustness of LLM-based multi-agent systems remains underexplored.

contributions.claim: RollMAS is a generalizable and computationally efficient protection mechanism for improving LLM-based multi-agent system robustness.
An action negotiation algorithm enables multiple local policies to converge through vector-space signal synchronization, mitigating risks from agent discrepancies.

A sharing redundancy enhancement algorithm maximizes an approximate natural eigenvalue of the corresponding adjacency matrix to support resilient and efficient information sharing with controlled communication overhead.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments across traffic control and question answering tasks, 7 datasets, and 13 baselines reportedly show substantial improvements in LLM-based multi-agent system robustness and effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems are attracting attention for handling complex tasks.
Existing research mainly addresses task-specific agent design, cooperation mechanisms, and pipeline optimization.
Robustness is underexplored, while agent conflicts and insufficient information sharing can cause global failures under abnormal or adversarial conditions.
RollMAS combines action negotiation with sharing redundancy enhancement to protect LLM-based multi-agent systems.
Experiments on traffic control and question answering across 7 datasets and 13 baselines reportedly demonstrate improved robustness and effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Synchronizing signals among multiple local policies and enhancing redundant information sharing are presented as mechanisms for improving multi-agent robustness.

interpretation.claim: Robustness may benefit from jointly reducing policy disagreement and increasing resilience in inter-agent communication.

application.claim: For multi-agent systems exposed to conflicting decisions or unreliable communication, consider coordination mechanisms alongside controlled redundancy in information sharing.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these mechanisms generalize beyond the reported traffic control and question answering tasks or how communication overhead is quantified.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, attack or abnormal-condition settings, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not report quantitative results or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not describe implementation details, computational costs, or the limits of generalizability.
